newsitem.title: SPAIN: Basque businessman feared kidnapped by rebels.
newsitem.headline: Basque businessman feared kidnapped by rebels.

text.p: A Basque businessman, missing since Monday, appears to have been kidnapped by separatist ETA rebels, the Spanish government said on Wednesday.

"All the clues point to a kidnapping," Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja told a radio interviewer when asked about the disappearance of businessman Cosme Delclaux, 34. "That's the most likely scenario."
Delclaux's family notified the police after waiting in vain for him to reappear on Monday, local media said.

Mayor Oreja said the apparent kidnapping confirmed there were no grounds to hope for a unilateral truce by ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom), which has staged only minor attacks in the last few months.
"We were witnessing some kind of mirage," he said of the lull. "There has been a mirage in some circles, but it's obvious that ETA is there."
The Basque separatists have killed nearly 800 people in a drive for full independence begun in 1968. They are currently holding a prisons officer who was abducted 10 months ago.
